full_judgment:
3. The case was filed on the allegation that the property in dispute originally belonged to Abdul Gani, who died leaving behind two sons named Kanchan Ali and Kashem Ali. Kanchan Ali died leaving behind 4 sons 3 daughters and one widow. The pre-emptors are 3 sons of Kanchan Ali and they have been in possession in their ancestral property of disputed SA khatian No. 580. The pre-emptors at first came to learn about kabala on 29-5-2005 from Alo Miah in presence of Kamrul and Somir that their uncle Kashem Ali sold 0.38 acre of land out of 0.60 acre to stranger opposite party No. 1 and got definite knowledge on 05-6-2005 after obtaining certified copy of the impugned document dated 11-5-1999. Pre-emptors had no knowledge of sale because no notice was served. The disputed land is necessary because it is adjacent to their homestead and they are co-sharers by inheritance. The disputed land is within the Barisal City Corporation hence the case was filed under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act. 

 4. The petitioner as opposite party No. 1 appeared and contested the case by filing written objection contending inter alia that Kashem Ali sold 0.38 acre of land to this petitioner by kabala dated 11-5-1999 and delivered possession. The pre-emptors had earlier knowledge and opposite party No. 1 purchased the land when the pre-emptors refused to purchase the same due to financial inability. Opposite party No. 1 mutated Khatian No. 4409 on 9-4-2004 and has been in possession upon payment of rent and also opened separate holding in the corporation. The land under pre-emption was low and it was filed up with earth and erected structure and let out 15 cubit tin-shed room with latrine and planted many valuable trees within the knowledge of the pre-emptors. The disputed land was acquired in LA Case No. 1 of 2004-2005 for the purpose of Dapdapia Bridge and opposite party No. 1 applied for compensation. The brother of the pre-emptors named Bazlur Rahman also sold his share on 30-4-2002 to some local persons but no pre-emption was filed against this document because the consideration is higher than the earlier disputed document dated 11-5-2009 and it was disputed document dated 11-5-2009 and it was further stated that the price of the land has increased noticeably and the pre-emptors being extremely greedy are out to get this valuable land at a low price and has filed this case with false story of knowledge which is liable to be dismissed; it was alleged that price of land increased abnormally by lapse of time. Immediately after sale there was chance of possession and change of nature and character within the knowledge of the pre-emptor opposite party. 

 12. He next submits that the learned appellate court upon misreading and non-consideration of material evidence failed to notice that the case land is next to homestead of the pre-emptor and opposite party has been in possession upon payment of rent Exhibit-Ga series according to Mutation Khatian Exhibit-ka and OPW-2 and OPW-3 are close neighbors of both the parties which was not denied at all by the pre-emptors and possession of opposite party for more than 6 years falsified the claim of knowledge thus the learned appellate court committed error of law occasioning failure of justice. 

 13. He further submits that the learned appellate court misread the evidence and wrongly found opposite party has not filed any document supporting mutation but Exhibit-ka itself is the mutation khatian and such misreading affecting the merit of the case shows that the learned court failed to apply judicial mind occasioning failure of justice. 

 27. He further submits that in the instant case. OPW 1 is the constituted Attorney of the petitioner she resides in America. If any improvement is made that is done at their risk. He also submits that there is no mention about the cost incurred towards development they done it at their own risk. This also no description of the quantum of land of the khatian and also no proof as regard withdrawal of the compensation money and also did not mention any date of withdrawal of the money. So the impugned judgment of the last court of fact does not suffer from any legal infirmity material irregularity and illegality for which the appellate court judgment can be interfered with in support of his contention he has referred the case of Anowara Khatun vs Md Abdul Hye and others reported in 5 BLC (AD) 14.
